cases.name: Donna Jean Atlas
cases.about: She was a microbiologist for the Department of Health and Environmental Sciences.

cases.name: Pamela Ann Dorrington
cases.about: She lived in her apartment with her cousin Mary Kay Dorrington and they both worked at St. Peters Hospital. She was a surgical technician and had an interest in Russia. She was described as very dependable, reliable and considerate of her parents.
cases.narrative:
In 6/16/1968, her torso from below her navel to her knees was found near the boat dock at Gates of the Mountains Marina in Helena, MT. In 2021, he confessed to strangling and sexually assaulting her, dismembering her and throwing her remains -- in a barrel -- off of York Bridge. There was clothing on her body which helped identify her.

On the day of her death, Dorrington was called by Atlas, who was her landlord at the time. He said there was a water leak in the apartment and wanted to repair it. Dorrington let him into her apartment and Atlas strangled her, Metcalf said.

He gathered a dress and sash. Metcalf said the sash was found with Dorrington's remains. He moved her downstairs, sexually assaulted her and then placed her body in a barrel.

He moved the barrel to an airplane hangar, where he taught flying lessons. He stored the body there while he taught students that day, then took the barrel in his vehicle to a remote area. He dismembered the body and threw the barrel off the York Bridge.

cases.name: Rebekah White-Roman
cases.about: Rebekah has worked for many years as a residential services specialist at Spring Meadow Resources, a Helena nonprofit that offers group homes and other services to those with disabilities. "She was just loved by so many people here and by our clients, and she will be missed. She was definitely a part of our family," said Jodie Lineaweaver, human resources specialist at Spring Meadow Resources. " ... She was a key part of what we do here and had such a love for our mission and our clients."
